product--01-quoin-payments.why: Dense, exact payments-matching table with one green accent: the bar the rest of the gallery is measured against.

product--02-fennick-approvals.why: Bill queue and approval panel with a ledger that adds up; quiet chrome, small exact type.

product--03-corvane-record.why: Company record with a real activity feed and field diffs; restrained and specific.

product--05-kilnworks-billing.why: Usage and billing with a forecast, a budget line and invoices; orange has one job.

product--04-sounding-observability.why: Strong service overview, let down by one synthetic-looking chart and one empty card.

product--06-ferrule-security.why: Clean security settings and audit log; the settings frame is long toggle rows, the audit frame is the stronger image.

styles--09-bento-grid.why: Holdfast help desk bento reads like a shipped SaaS page and beat Windsurf's bento in the blind test, but every tile is full.

styles--12-pixel-art.why: A believable live-ops dashboard where the pixel theme carries data; it won its blind pair, but every region is packed.

styles--07-risograph.why: Real editorial study with data in the inks, but the hero numbers collide and the page uses too many text sizes.

styles--04-skeuomorphism.why: Convincing post-production console, but nearly every pixel is a control and the chrome reads as a plugin skin.

styles--11-terminal.why: Consistent man-page style, but one monospace face flattens the hierarchy, and the gallery image is out of date.

styles--01-glassmorphism.why: A real asset-review product on a real photo, but placeholder bars on the photo read as an unfinished wireframe.

styles--10-mesh-gradient.why: Good eval product UI; the mesh gradient became a glowing orange blob in the chart.

styles--05-comic.why: Distinctive and data-carrying, but three faces and dense halftone panels make it look busy and amateur next to shipped editorial pages.

styles--08-bauhaus.why: The shapes carry data, but they bleed off the bottom so the page looks cropped, not composed.

styles--06-memphis.why: Ticket shapes sized by sales are good, but the hero uses the floating, tilted fragment tell.

styles--02-neumorphism.why: The floor plan is hundreds of tiny boxes and the one neumorphic element is grey on grey.

styles--03-claymorphism.why: Clean checklist, but the clay avatar and lanyard badge look like stock AI renders.

heroes--08-y2k-retrofuture.why: One object made with care and a confident display word; the owner calls it good to go.

heroes--14-fennick-approvals.why: The ledger-led B2B hero beat Coda's hero by a clear margin, but its product frame repeats product/02.

heroes--11-spend-platform.why: Ramp-grade spend hero that won its blind pair; the chart and header are crowded.

heroes--02-luminous-devtool.why: A real search console that won its blind pair, with a dead hole on the left and a big-stat recipe.

heroes--01-swiss-architecture.why: A confident section drawing that carries data; it won its blind pair but has too many annotation layers.

heroes--07-climate-observatory.why: Real science UI that won its blind pair, but contour texture runs behind the text.

heroes--03-organic-wellness.why: Nice serif headline, but the tin and flowers look like clip-art and a quarter of the frame is empty.

heroes--12-sounding-observability.why: Repeats product/04 pixel for pixel and lost its blind pair; the product section already shows this screen better.

heroes--13-ferrule-security.why: Repeats product/06's audit frame, and the spaced headline reads as a layout bug.

components--02-command-palette.why: The palette itself is premium; the owner's one approved component. Drop the spec-sheet half.

components--08-music-player.why: Rebuilt dark listening room; the judge called it equal to SoundCloud on craft.

components--07-ai-composer.why: Rebuilt composer is clean and specific, but it floats in empty space and reads like Claude Projects.

components--09-onboarding-stepper.why: Rebuilt as a Sedge payroll setup: believable B2B, but every element has a grey second line and it reads as Gusto.

components--03-date-range-picker.why: Rebuilt as a Gridlark dashboard picker; tidy, but the popover shows everything at once.

components--06-data-table.why: Rebuilt shipments table (re-rendered 05:59) is tidy, but uniform demo data and stacked chrome make it read as a well-made fake.

components--01-pricing-glass.why: Rebuilt pricing is tidy but generic dark-SaaS, and it stacks notes before the features.

components--10-settings-terminal.why: Rebuilt as Ackwire notification settings; competent, but one modal holds too much.

components--05-toast-stack.why: Rebuilt at 06:02 as Panelwise, a hiring pipeline with a toast stack; cleaner than the Slack clone it replaced, but the toasts bury the table.

components--04-upload-brutal.why: Half the frame is a spec sheet and the rest is boxed decoration.

app-screens--05-travel-boarding.why: The owner's 'great': clear, real and calm. Fix one weekday.

app-screens--04-fitness-neon.why: The owner's 'great': condensed numerals, one lime accent, live data.

app-screens--11-approvals-mobile.why: Reads like a shipped enterprise iOS app, but has no voice of its own.

app-screens--08-podcast-player.why: Nice transcript idea, but the serif title dominates and the pause button looks unstyled.

app-screens--07-language-lesson.why: Well executed, but a viewer names Duolingo in one second.

app-screens--03-recipe-editorial.why: Real photo and serif title, but the palette and spacing feel cheap (the owner asked for better fonts and spacing).

app-screens--06-plant-care.why: Real plant photos and believable data, but three type voices and a crowded first card.

app-screens--09-project-workspace.why: A Linear clone with a heavy grey Gantt; the judge named Linear at once.

app-screens--10-clinical-vitals.why: The owner's 'needs a lot of work': every value boxed in caramel, like spreadsheet formatting.

app-screens--01-private-banking.why: The owner's 'fonts are not visible': a Didone total fights the UI text, grey on charcoal, a bare polyline chart.

watch--09-oncall-incident.why: Useful and clear, but four lines at nearly one size and buttons that press the edge.

watch--01-ridgeline-trail.why: Strong pace number, but three faces and decorative chart texture.

watch--07-leeward-sail.why: A real instrument, but all-mono type and a dial cut by the screen edge.

watch--05-nook-home.why: Reads as Apple Home tiles with a glaring gradient.

watch--04-headway-transit.why: Clear idea, default-looking condensed type and many small marks.

watch--02-thrum-heart.why: The heart-rate number is crammed and the bottom is a decorative gradient line.

watch--03-tidemark-face.why: Elegant time, but a painted sky-and-sea gradient stands in for an asset.

watch--08-onething-focus.why: A generic focus timer with a reused number; nothing only this brand could own.

footers--02-keystrata-mega.why: The owner's approved enterprise mega footer.

footers--08-rallo-app.why: The owner approved it, but it carries invented proof and four decorations at once.

footers--09-b2b-platform.why: Close to Railway or Vercel, but a loud amber date and three mini-tables crowd it.

footers--05-salt-ledger-index.why: The issue-spine chart is lovely, but the footer does a homepage's job.

footers--07-sasame-tea.why: Elegant type, but most of the footer is a Gantt chart with untidy details.

footers--04-tumbletree-meadow.why: Real content (letter formation), but a kids' brand on corporate navy with a crowded diagram.

footers--06-knurl-brutalist.why: Every element boxed with an offset shadow, four decorations at once, and a wrong weekday.

mockups--10-multi-device.why: Flat and legible, but a presentation plate with a caption strip and dead space.

mockups--09-laptop-dashboard.why: The best design in the gallery on a laptop, at a size where none of it reads.

mockups--07-tablet-clinic.why: Shows the Wardlight screen, which scores 4 here; re-render after that rebuild.

mockups--01-phone-trio.why: Two of its three phones show pieces the owner rejected.

mockups--05-components-board.why: Shows the old web components the owner calls rubbish.

mockups--08-made-with-opendesigner.why: Its grid shows heroes the owner removed as 'very ugly'.

mockups--04-browser-cascade.why: Shows a removed hero and a replaced hero, with numbered documentation callouts.

mockups--06-poster-street.why: A billboard of a hero the owner removed as 'very ugly'.
